author: M. C. Buckner
title: Judge finds Raymond Link guilty but mentally ill in Petersen Park attempted murder case
text:
Judge finds Raymond Link guilty but mentally ill in Petersen Park attempted murder case
Raymond Link, 49, of West Allis, Wisconsin, was found guilty but mentally ill of attempted first-degree murder and six counts of aggravated battery after a bench trial before Judge Tiffany E. Davis on June 24 at the McHenry County courthouse. Sentencing is scheduled for September 2.
Evidence at trial showed that on May 25, 2024, a woman walking her dog in Petersen Park in McHenry was violently assaulted by Link. The attack involved beating, stomping, and strangling the victim with bare hands and nearly resulted in her death. The assault ended when a bystander intervened while calling 911. When confronted by the bystander, Link claimed he was performing CPR on the victim; however, as the bystander approached further, he saw Link kick the victim in the head. Link then attacked the bystander and ordered his dog to attack as well. The bystander suffered a broken clavicle and multiple dog bite injuries while trying to protect the woman.
McHenry Police Department officers responded quickly and took Link into custody at the scene. As a result of the attack, according to prosecutors, the victim suffered catastrophic injuries including loss of an eye, multiple broken bones, and permanent brain damage.
At trial, Link asserted an insanity defense. Judge Davis rejected this defense after considering all testimony and evidence presented during proceedings. Under Illinois law, being found guilty but mentally ill does not relieve criminal responsibility; such defendants face penalties equivalent to other convicted offenders.
“This was a horrific act of violence that forever changed the lives of two innocent people,” said State’s Attorney Randi L. Freese. “The victim endured unimaginable injuries, and a brave citizen put himself in harm’s way to intervene and help save her life.” Freese also commended Chief of Staff Ashley Romito for prosecuting what she described as an extraordinarily complex case involving significant questions about mental state and criminal responsibility: “Our office is fortunate to have Chief of Staff Ashley Romito... We are grateful for her exceptional work...”
Freese also acknowledged support from Victim Advocate Kelly Gallagher throughout proceedings as well as investigative efforts from McHenry Police Department.
The average student-to-teacher ratio in McHenry County was 14-to-1 during the 2022-23 school year with over 45 thousand students enrolled across county schools; Huntley High School had both the highest white student enrollment (2,133) and multiracial student enrollment (135), Harvard High School had the highest Hispanic enrollment (574), Harry D. Jacobs High School had the highest Black enrollment (87), while teacher absenteeism stood at just over thirty-four percent—slightly below state average—according to data from Illinois State Board of Education.
